epp:phrases.epp:phrase: The metadata is completed and there are no files to upload because this is not a repository. Now deposit the item.

The title should not end with a full stop, but may end with a question mark. There is no way to make italic text, please enter it normally. If there is a subtitle, it should be preceded with a colon [:]. Use sentence case, i.e. lower case letters throughout except for the first word and for proper nouns.
Example: The role of construction project managers in design management
Example: Construction claims management in Nigeria: Does information technology help?

A summary of the item's content. If the item has a formal abstract then that is what should be entered here. No complicated text formatting is possible. Please remove all paragraph breaks and any extraneous information. Only the text of the abstract should be here.

Enter the family name in the first box, given names in the second box. If possible, provide the full given names rather than mere initials, to help distinguish different authors with common family names. Leave the email addresses blank. If there are more than four authors, click on the button.
Example: [Smith] [J.P.] [ omit email addresses ]
Example: [Chance-Collins] [Chris] [ ]
Example: [Fu] [Yan-Li] [ ]
Example: [von Höpfner] [Ludwig G.] [ ]

These are not authors. For journal papers, leave blank. Typically, they will only be used for theses. Enter contributors' names along with type of contribution selected from the drop-down list, usually [ Thesis advisor ]
If there are more than four contributors, click on the button.

Please indicate whether this version of the work been refereed below. Any journal paper added to the database must have been refereed. For example, editorial articles will not be added to the database.
Enter the volume number of the journal or series in which the item appeared.
Any comments to the database administrator. This information will not be displayed to the public.

The date this journal paper was published, or the date of award for a PhD. Unpublished or unfinished items are not included in this database.
The event to which the date applies. Always select [ Publication ] for journal papers and [ Completed ] for PhD theses.

Please confirm here that the item has been published. However, doctoral theses are technically [ Unpublished ] unless there is a URL, in which case they are readily available and deemed to be [ Published ], although that word is omitted from the formatted reference.

The canonical (permanent) URL for this item. Everything entered into this database is expected to have a URL.
Example: https://www.greatjournal.com/2003/983241/

Numerals only. The sequence of pages of the paper. Do not enter pp. Omit page range for doctoral theses.
Example: 21 to 34

The title of a journal, publication or magazine. Capitalise each word, except for short words like "in", "of", "and", "for".
Example: Construction Management and Risk

A person, firm or corporate body responsible for placing an item on the market. Do not use abbreviations, enter in full.
Example: Oxford University Press

Natural language terms to describe the content of the item. All in lower case, please, except where there are acronyms, which should not be encouraged as keywords, due to their ambiguity. This is not the place to define acronyms.
Omit phrases that apply to every paper in the database, such as construction management.

p.small: N.B. Index terms, topics, subjects and descriptive scope are assigned automatically, by matching words in title, abstract and keywords against the taxonomy. They record the vocabulary of the paper, not a judgement on the research. If the coding looks questionable, please get in touch. More on index terms and descriptive scope.

epp:phrase.div: Each topic names a problem or phenomenon addressed in the items listed here. Items may appear under more than one topic, so the counts overlap.

ul.li: Entering the same term in more than one field restricts the search to results present in ALL those fields, like AND. At the bottom of the fields list, there is an option to change this to search for any condition rather than all conditions (Retrieved records must fulfill:). You can also change the sequence in which the results are presented (the default is chronological).

Within most of the search fields, there is a drop-down menu. The default is "all of". Its effect is:
All of these words: matches only if all appear (like AND)
Any of these words: matches if any appear (like OR)
Quotation marks are ignored. For example, searching for "urban development" is the same as searching for urban development, i.e., two separate words.
Common short words, called "stop words" (e.g., and, or, the), are ignored and cannot be used as Boolean operators.
After your first search, you can use "Refine Search" to narrow results further by adding more 'all of' filters or expanding them as needed.

div.p: There is also an option to undertake a Basic Search, at the top right of most screens in this site. This automatically searches all indexed fields such as authors, titles, author names and abstracts, but not journal titles and it behaves differently from Advanced Search in some respects - see the user documentation.

If you have any questions about the database, or suggestions for improving it, please get in touch. We welcome feedback from researchers, students, practitioners, and anyone with an interest in construction management research; including anyone involved in cataloguing, indexing, or managing similar databases in other topic areas.

These explanatory notes and commentaries have been written by Prof Will Hughes as the curator of the site and they reflect his personal understanding and interpretation. They are offered to clarify the structure and intent of the catalogue and to encourage thoughtful discussion.
